info.name: BugTrail APIs
info.description:
BugTrail API, grouped by module. Start the API (`npm run dev`) and create the Admin (`npm run seed`), then:

1. Set the collection variables `adminEmail` / `adminPassword` to the Admin you created in the seed.
2. **Auth → Login** (saves `accessToken`).
3. Anything else. Ids created along the way (`userId`, `pendingUserId`, `projectId`, `bugId`) are saved automatically.
Or just **Run collection**: the folders are ordered so a full top-to-bottom run passes against a freshly seeded API.

Roles are fixed values: admin, project_manager, developer, ui_ux, qa. What each role can do is defined in code
(see **Roles → Access catalog**); permissions are never sent in requests.

Every request sends `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}` (collection-level auth) unless it says "No auth".
The refresh token is an httpOnly cookie: Postman keeps it in its cookie jar, so **Auth → Refresh tokens** works like a browser.
When the access token expires (30 min) you get 401: run Refresh tokens or Login again.

Swagger with full schemas: {{baseUrl}}/docs (development only).

item.name: Auth
item.description: Login, session refresh (httpOnly cookie), registration, password flows and the current user.

request.description: Returns the user (with role and permissions) and an access token; sets the `refreshToken` httpOnly cookie. Pending/suspended/rejected accounts get 403.
Current user with role and the permissions it grants.
No body: uses the `refreshToken` cookie from Login and rotates it.
Creates a `pending` user with no role. designation (job title) is required. They can log in only after Users → Approve pending user.
Signs out other sessions and keeps this one (new cookie + access token). Followed by "Change password back" so the seed Admin keeps its password.
Restores adminPassword so the collection can be re-run.
Always 204. With SMTP_HOST empty the reset link is printed in the API console: copy its token into `resetToken`.

Sets a new password and signs out every session. Skipped automatically while `resetToken` is empty (copy it from the API console after Forgot password). Remember to update `adminPassword` after using it.

Revokes the refresh token in the cookie and clears it. Idempotent. Note: the access token stays valid until it expires (max 30 min). Access tokens are stateless, which is why they are short-lived. The web app simply forgets it.

item.name: Roles
item.description: Roles are a fixed list on the user (no roles table); permissions follow from the role. Read-only catalog served from code.

request.description: Every role (admin, project_manager, developer, ui_ux, qa) with what each can do, plus the grouped permission labels. Any signed-in user.

item.name: Users
item.description: User management, the approval queue and your own profile.

request.description: Requires `user:read`. Filters: search (part of the name or email, case-insensitive), name (exact), role (admin | project_manager | developer | ui_ux | qa), status. Each row is the summary plus createdAt and lastLoginAt.
Requires `bug:read`. Everyone a bug can be assigned to: active users whose role can work on bugs, sorted by name. Assigning a bug to someone who is not on the project adds them as a member.
Requires `user:create`. Created active. Permissions follow from the role.

Requires `user:update`. Changing the role changes what the user can do on their next request. You can't manage a user with permissions you don't hold, or change your own role. Setting `password` signs the user out.
pending → rejected. A rejected user can still be approved later (next request).
Requires `user:approve`. pending/rejected → active needs a role. Run Auth → Register first to fill `pendingUserId`.
Ends their sessions immediately. The last active Admin can never be suspended.
Keeps the role the user had.
Name and avatar only. Password → Auth → Change password.
Requires `user:delete`. You can't delete yourself or the last active Admin. Prefer suspending.

item.name: Projects
item.description: Projects, members and the bug summary behind each card's pie. You see the projects you're a member of; Admin (project:read_all) sees all. A project outside your scope is a 404.

request.description: Requires `project:create` (Admin). `key` (2-10 letters/digits, starts with a letter) prefixes every bug key (BT-42); stored uppercase, unique, never changes. Optional: `manager` (a PM or Admin, auto-added as member), `members` (active user ids), `status`.

exec: for (let i = 0; i < 5; i += 1) { key += letters[Math.floor(Math.random() * letters.length)]; }

request.description: Requires `project:read`. Filters: status (active | completed | archived), search (name or key). Each item has `bugSummary` (byStatus counts, open count and the 3-slice `pie`).
Detail with description, manager and members.

Requires `project:update` (PM within their projects, Admin). Name, description, status, manager. The key can't change; a new manager (PM or Admin) who isn't a member yet is added. status archived makes the project read-only.
Requires `project:manage_members`. Idempotent; only active users. Uses the user approved in Users → Approve user. Returns the full member list.
Distinct module/screen names used in the project's bugs, for the report form. Empty here: see Bugs.
The project manager can't be removed; change the manager first. Returns the full member list.
Requires `project:delete` (Admin). Soft delete: hidden everywhere, history kept, key stays reserved.

item.name: Bugs
item.description: Tickets, the status workflow, assignment and the timeline. Self-contained: it creates its own project, walks one bug through the whole lifecycle (including a QA fail) and cleans up. As Admin every move is allowed; the bug's `allowedStatuses` shows what the current user may do. A developer (the assignee) may only do reported → ongoing → resolved and failed → ongoing.

Requires `bug:read`. Filters: status (comma-separated), assignee (id | me | none), moduleName, search (title/module, or a key like BT-42). sortBy: age | failCount | updatedAt | createdAt | bugNumber. Without projectId: every project you can see.

item.name: Chat
item.description: Messages on a bug. Saved through REST, then broadcast over Socket.IO to everyone with the bug open (message:new / message:updated / message:deleted). To watch them live, run `npm run realtime:listen -- <accessToken> <bugId>` in a terminal while you send these. Self-contained: creates a project and a bug, then cleans up.

request.description: The assignee (the developer approved in Users) gets a bug_assigned notification.
Requires `chat:send`. Mentions must be project members (others are ignored). Mentioned users get bug_mentioned; the assignee and reporter get bug_message, except whoever has the bug open right now.
Requires `chat:read`. Oldest first within the page. If `nextCursor` isn't null, load older messages with `?before={nextCursor}`.
Your own messages only (403 otherwise). Sets `editedAt`; mentions aren't re-notified.
Your own messages only. It stays in the thread as a tombstone: `deleted: true`, `body: null`.

item.name: Notifications
item.description: Your bell: always your own notifications. New ones also arrive live as `notification:new`. Auth → Register gave the Admin a "waiting for approval" notification, so this folder has something to show.

request.description: Newest first. `?unread=true` for unread only. Each has `link` (a web app path) and `entity`.
Skipped when you have no notifications yet.

item.name: Dashboard
item.description: Dashboard numbers, limited to the projects you can see. Filters on every request: `projectId`, `from` / `to` (when the bug was reported: `2026-10-12` or an ISO date-time; a date-only `to` covers the whole day, UTC). The other folders clean up after themselves, so on a fresh database most numbers are 0: report a few bugs to see them move.

request.description: Requires `dashboard:view`. Projects by status, and bugs by status with total/open and the pie.
Bugs reported in 2026. Project counts are not date-filtered.
Requires `dashboard:view_performance` (QA, PM, Admin). Per current assignee: assigned, open, passed, totalFails, firstPassRate, avgTimeToPassMs.
Top tickets by age (reported until passed, or now). `open=true` leaves out passed ones.
